aggregation.answerUnit: One reader answer scored by the other model only; self-judging is forbidden.
aggregation.caseArm: Arithmetic mean of the MiniMax-reader/DeepSeek-judge score and the DeepSeek-reader/MiniMax-judge score.
aggregation.population: Arithmetic mean of case-arm scores over the frozen 200-case census.
aggregation.fama: For each judged answer, MPA minus lambda times one minus FAA, clipped at zero; lambda is forgetting criteria divided by all criteria. The two crossed-reader FAMA scores are then averaged per case-arm before population aggregation.

protocol.decisionRule: A challenger is promoted only if every predeclared full-population quality, uncertainty, cost and integrity gate passes. Subgroups explain mechanisms but cannot override a failed primary gate.

reuse.rule: Reuse is allowed only for byte-identical reader message arrays within the same frozen case.

protocol.claimBoundary: This panel tests robustness and causal policy factors on previously unconsumed Memora questions. It is not a pristine dataset holdout, a human evaluation, or evidence about real programming-agent traffic.

caveats: This panel tests robustness and causal policy factors on previously unconsumed Memora questions. It is not a pristine dataset holdout, a human evaluation, or evidence about real programming-agent traffic.
The 200 questions were not used by either prior answer-level panel, but quarterly Memora had already been observed during earlier proxy development.
Only six cases expose obsolete evidence in Base top-5 under the released labels; full-population effects are therefore expected to be diluted and are the primary robustness estimate.
Cross-model judging avoids self-judging, but it is not a substitute for blinded human correctness calibration.
Simple baselines and ablations use the same frozen FTS candidate pool, prompt template, readers, crossed judges, criteria and case census.
